Fit the detection link: how a cell's latent value sets the chance that a trial succeeds

stats_fit_link.Rd

Fit the detection link of a latent-scale mixed model (how a cell's latent value, such as the log-odds of a site's occupancy, sets the chance that a trial succeeds) by maximum likelihood over cells with a latent mean and SD and a count.

Answers how does a count's chance of success follow the latent value? mzLib's LogitNormalMixedModel.FitLink (mzLib #1469) finds the DetectionLink - logit g = intercept + slope x latent + depth_slope x depth - that makes your cells' counts most likely, each cell's latent value taken as a normal with the mean and SD you give, by maximum likelihood. By default it fits on detection: whether any trial succeeded, which is what makes a covered zero. Pass the result to stats_fit_latent_mixed as link.

Usage

stats_fit_link(cells, with_depth = NULL, with_overdispersion = NULL,
  detection_only = NULL, timeout = 600)

Arguments

cells

A TSV whose header names latent_mean, latent_sd, successes and trials, and optionally depth, in any order and no other column: one row per covered cell. The latent mean and SD are in latent units, successes of trials is the cell's count, and depth is in your depth units. Without a depth column every depth is mzLib's default (0 at the pin).

with_depth

Fit the depth slope (mzLib's withDepth). NULL (the default) sends nothing: mzLib's declared default (FALSE at the pin), which with_depth in the result reports.

with_overdispersion

Fit rho, the beta-binomial correlation of the trials in a cell (mzLib's withOverdispersion). NULL (the default): mzLib's declared default (FALSE at the pin).

detection_only

TRUE fits on whether any trial succeeded, FALSE on the full counts (mzLib's detectionOnly). NULL (the default): mzLib's declared default (TRUE at the pin).

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

A slope below 1 says the chance of a success rises more slowly than the latent: on PTM data, for example, whether a modified form is seen depends on how much of it there is, not only on its share. The cells, and their latent means and SDs, are your choice: mzLibR does not build them. mzLib's own example is a covered cell's feature mean and SD over its measured cells.

Value

An mzlibr_link_fit: cells_file, the cells table's absolute path; cell_count, rows read (cells); depth_given, whether the cells file has a depth column; with_depth, with_overdispersion and detection_only, as passed: what you gave, else mzLib's declared default; link, the fitted mzlibr_detection_link, ready for stats_fit_latent_mixed's link, or NULL when mzLib's search did not converge - intercept (natural log-odds, the per-trial log-odds at latent 0 and depth 0), slope (natural log-odds per latent unit), depth_slope (natural log-odds per depth unit; exactly 0 when with_depth is FALSE) and overdispersion (fraction, the intra-cell correlation, 0 to below 1; exactly 0 when with_overdispersion is FALSE); and caveats, what the fit is and is not.

What it is not

A point estimate only: mzLib returns no standard errors. The cells and their latent normals are modelling choices, and the link fitted from them is only as good as they are. With with_depth = TRUE and no depth column, every depth is 0 and the data say nothing about depth_slope.

Wraps

Wire verb stats fit-link. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.fit-link.yaml (bridge commit aea14604d5f7) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • LogitNormalMixedModel.FitLink in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LogitNormalMixedModel.cs at mzLib cc67b7a2

  • LinkCell in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LogitNormalMixedModel.cs at mzLib cc67b7a2

  • DetectionLink in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LogitNormalMixedModel.cs at mzLib cc67b7a2

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

cells

path; required; range >= 1 row. A TSV with a header row naming the columns latent_mean, latent_sd, successes and trials, and optionally depth, in any order and no other (so a misspelt optional column cannot fall back to the default silently), then one row per covered cell (mzLib's LinkCell). latent_mean and latent_sd are the normal the cell's latent value is taken to sit at, in latent units (e.g. the mean and SD of its feature's measured cells, mzLib's example); successes of trials is its count; depth is in the caller's depth unit. Without a depth column every cell is constructed without one, so its depth is LinkCell's own default (0 at cc67b7a2). mzLib refuses a cell with a latent mean, SD or depth that is not finite, an SD below 0, no trials, or more successes than trials. Which cells, and their latent normals, are the caller's modelling choices.

with_depth (wire --with-depth)

bool; default absent; range true | false. mzLib's withDepth: fit the depth slope (else it is 0). Absent, the bridge passes FitLink's declared default (false at cc67b7a2), read from mzLib, and echoes it.

with_overdispersion (wire --with-overdispersion)

bool; default absent; range true | false. mzLib's withOverdispersion: fit the beta-binomial intra-cell correlation rho (else it is 0, binomial). Absent, FitLink's declared default (false at cc67b7a2), echoed.

detection_only (wire --detection-only)

bool; default absent; range true | false. mzLib's detectionOnly. true: fit on whether any trial succeeded, P(k = 0) against P(k >= 1), the event that makes a covered zero. false: fit on the full count, P(k of n). Absent, FitLink's declared default (true at cc67b7a2), echoed. mzLib's documentation: on PTM data the full counts follow occupancy more weakly than detection does, and a link fitted on them predicts covered zeros worse.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

cells_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the cells table.

cell_count

int; in cells; never NA. Rows read.

depth_given

bool; never NA. Whether the cells file has a depth column.

with_depth

bool; never NA. withDepth as passed: the option given, else mzLib's declared default.

with_overdispersion

bool; never NA. withOverdispersion as passed: the option given, else mzLib's declared default.

detection_only

bool; never NA. detectionOnly as passed: the option given, else mzLib's declared default.

link

object; NA when mzLib's search did not converge within its iteration limit (FitLink returned null). The fitted DetectionLink, ready for stats fit-latent-mixed --link; fields under result.tables.link.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Three static caveats (one says which likelihood was fitted), plus one each when the depth slope or overdispersion was not fitted, when the depth slope was fitted without a depth column, and when the search did not converge.

Fields of link

an mzlibr_detection_link, a named list of these four numbers.

link$intercept (wire intercept)

float; in natural log-odds; never NA. a: the per-trial log-odds at latent 0 and depth 0.

link$slope (wire slope)

float; in natural log-odds per latent unit; never NA. b: how fast the per-trial log-odds follow the latent. Below 1, the chance of a success rises more slowly than the latent.

link$depth_slope (wire depth_slope)

float; in natural log-odds per depth unit; never NA. c: the depth term's coefficient; exactly 0 when with_depth is false.

link$overdispersion (wire overdispersion)

float; in fraction (intra-cell correlation, 0 to < 1); never NA. rho, the correlation of trials within a cell; exactly 0 when with_overdispersion is false.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--cells missing, blank or not found; the table empty or header-only; a header with an empty, repeated, missing or unknown column (each named); a row whose field count differs from its header; a latent_mean, latent_sd or depth that is not a number (blank, NA or NaN pass to mzLib); successes or trials not a whole number; --with-depth, --with-overdispersion or --detection-only other than true or false, or without a value

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the cells (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a latent mean, SD or depth that is not finite, an SD below 0, no trials, or successes outside 0 to trials

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Maximum likelihood over the cells, each cell's probability integrated over its latent normal by 12-node adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature and maximized by Nelder-Mead. mzLib returns the point estimate only: no standard errors.

  • By default the fit is on detection (any success or none), not on how many trials succeeded: on PTM data, mzLib's documentation says, the full counts follow occupancy more weakly and predict covered zeros worse.

  • The link is in natural log-odds and is what stats fit-latent-mixed --link takes. Which cells enter, and their latent means and SDs, are the caller's modelling choices; the bridge builds neither.

  • With --with-depth true and no depth column, every cell's depth is 0 and the data say nothing about depth_slope.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.stats.fit_link

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::stats::fit_link_with with FitLinkOptions

  • R (mzLibR): stats_fit_link

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.7.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

References

  • doi:10.1093/comjnl/7.4.308: the simplex search mzLib maximizes the link's likelihood with (Nelder and Mead, Comput J 7:308, 1965)

  • doi:10.1093/biomet/81.3.624: adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature, which integrates each cell's probability over its latent normal (Liu and Pierce, Biometrika 81:624, 1994)

  • doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1948.tb00014.x: the beta-binomial distribution, the count model with overdispersion (Skellam, J R Stat Soc B 10:257, 1948)

See also

stats_fit_latent_mixed

Examples


# mzLib's own test cells: 4,000 cells simulated through the link (-0.5, 0.5, 0.3), which this
# package ships. The link is recovered from detection alone:
cells <- system.file("extdata", "stats", "link_cells.tsv", package = "mzLibR")
fit <- stats_fit_link(cells, with_depth = TRUE)
fit
#> <mzlibr_link_fit> 4000 cells, fitted on detection (any success or none)
#>   logit g = -0.5108 + 0.5065 x latent + 0.3313 x depth, overdispersion 0
round(unlist(fit$link), 2)
#>      intercept          slope    depth_slope overdispersion 
#>          -0.51           0.51           0.33           0.00
